trust_decision.summary: Whether an extension taken from untrusted metadata may become an on-disk file suffix is decided by one data allowlist, _UnsafeExtensionError.ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, consumed by sanitize_extension and applied through _change_extension; a single call site (_write_link_file) is exempted explicitly with the new _allowed_exts override. The fix is a data change, not a new check.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary says 'insufficient filename sanitization'; the sanitizer's policy table is ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS, which still lists 'desktop' (5214), 'url' (5218) and 'webloc' (5219). An engineer reading only the summary greps for the sanitizer and lands on this frozenset.

fix_sites.entry_point: yt_dlp.utils.replace_extension / prepend_extension (public library API) and every CLI path that names an output file
yt_dlp.utils.replace_extension / prepend_extension (public library API, signature extended with _allowed_exts)
_UnsafeExtensionError.sanitize_extension (classmethod consumed by all filename-building call sites)
CLI --write-link / --write-url-link / --write-webloc-link / --write-desktop-link, and the YoutubeDL.process_info public API

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The extractor package independently re-applies the same ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS test when it copies an extension out of a URL for a direct link (determine_ext(url) then `if ext not in _UnsafeExtensionError.ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS: ext = 'unknown_video'`); a solver who adds a denylist inside sanitize_extension sees that guard, sees it is in a different package the report never mentions, and concludes that route is already covered.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Internet-shortcut writing must keep working: --write-link/--write-url-link/--write-webloc-link/--write-desktop-link deliberately produce .url/.desktop/.webloc files from LINK_TEMPLATES (yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:4618-4622). Deleting the three entries from ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS without threading an override makes _change_extension raise _UnsafeExtensionError, which _catch_unsafe_extension_error (yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:186-197) turns into a report_error and a silent abort of the whole video's processing. A second coupled path: --compat-options allow-unsafe-ext monkeypatches the method with `lambda x, prepend=False: x` (yt_dlp/__init__.py:618-622), so the published fix's new `_allowed_exts=` keyword raises TypeError on that documented option.

O6_input_shapes: replace_extension where the trailing component matches expected_real_ext: final suffix is replaced and sanitized non-prepend
replace_extension where expected_real_ext is absent or does not match: the dangerous value is appended as a second suffix after the existing one
prepend_extension (prepend=True): the value becomes an infix before the preserved real suffix, so no allowlist test is applied at all

multi-component values whose only checked part is the text after the last dot (subtitles_filename passes `sub_lang + '.' + sub_format` at yt_dlp/utils/_utils.py:1321-1322; thumbnails pass `f'{t["id"]}.{thumb_ext}'` at yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:4502)
extension containing '/' or '\\' (rejected unconditionally, before the allowlist test)
case variants (compared with last.lower()) and the 'bin' -> 'unknown_video' remap
per-call-site override: `_allowed_exts=()` default everywhere vs `_allowed_exts=tuple(LINK_TEMPLATES)` for the link writer

O7_producer.where: yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:4376 (_write_info_json writes the info dict, including 'ext') and yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:3693-3702 (download_with_info_file reloads that JSON straight into process_ie_result)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Default output template: `%(ext)s` is substituted straight from info_dict['ext'] into the filename; _prepare_filename only calls replace_extension when final_ext or OUTTMPL_TYPES[force_ext] is set, so the allowlist is never consulted for the main media file
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The value comes from an extractor's own format selection rather than from the user or a link, and the obvious attacker-controlled variant (a direct link) is already guarded at extractor/generic.py:907, so it reads as trusted metadata
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file as the link-write site, ~1900 lines away, in a different function family (outtmpl evaluation vs process_info)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: --load-info-json reloads an info dict from an arbitrary JSON file and feeds its 'ext' through process_ie_result -> process_info -> prepare_filename with no allowlist consult anywhere on the way
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Loading a local JSON file is an explicit, advanced user choice ('created with --write-info-json'), so it is treated as trusted input and as a legacy/debug path rather than an attack surface
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~300 lines below the link-write site; the writing half is _write_info_json at yt_dlp/YoutubeDL.py:4376

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Merge path builds the output name by raw string concatenation, `f'{filename_wo_ext}.{ext}'` in the local correct_ext helper, never calling sanitize_extension
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Only used when separate video and audio formats are merged, and the extension is then rewritten by ffmpeg, so it reads as an unsupported combination rather than a file-creation sink
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, ~80 lines below the link-write site

O8_uncovered_routes.route: --compat-options allow-unsafe-ext replaces sanitize_extension wholesale with an identity lambda, so every site above becomes unchecked
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Documented with a warning as an opt-in escape hatch (README.md:2354), so the user is understood to have asked for it and it is treated as out of scope by construction
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: different file from the landing point, in the CLI entry module; the documented exception sits in README.md

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new OUTTMPL_TYPES entry with a forced extension (like 'annotation': 'annotations.xml') for another sidecar file
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Named-file types are a one-line dict entry, and _prepare_filename immediately routes every such entry through replace_extension(filename, force_ext, ...), so a maintainer adding a new sidecar kind naturally inherits the same sink

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A fourth internet-shortcut kind (e.g. a .website/.inetloc-style file) added to LINK_TEMPLATES and to the write_links dict
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: write_links is an open registry and the published fix auto-exempts exactly `tuple(LINK_TEMPLATES)`, so adding a key to both tables is all a maintainer would do to ship a new shortcut format

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Another OS-interpreted extension added to the 'others' section of ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS (the way 'm3u', 'sbv' and 'ism' already are)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The allowlist is a flat hand-maintained table with no per-entry justification, so a maintainer fixing a user report about a downloaded playlist/subtitle file would simply append the extension

O9_family: unsafe file-type/name restriction (CWE-641): an allowlist of permitted output extensions that still admits OS-interpreted types

O10_build.toolchain: no compile step; pure Python, hatchling packaging, optional ffmpeg/JS runtime binaries for some features
O10_build.project_tests: test/test_utils.py:302-346 covers prepend_extension/replace_extension and _UnsafeExtensionError (self._uncommon_extensions at :302-307); test/test_YoutubeDL.py has no --write-link or link-file tests, and the fix diff adds no tests

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete 'url', 'desktop' and 'webloc' from ALLOWED_EXTENSIONS and stop, which silently kills --write-link/--write-*-link (the error is swallowed as an abort) and leaves the raw %(ext)s / --load-info-json / correct_ext routes untouched
